facts.statement: The genus Caseosaurus was formally described and named by Hunt, Lucas, Heckert, Sullivan, and Lockley in 1998.
facts.quote: Caseosaurus was described, and named by A. P. Hunt, Spencer G. Lucas, Andrew B. Heckert, Robert M. Sullivan, and Martin Lockley in 1998

facts.statement: Caseosaurus was a small, lightly built, bipedal, ground-dwelling carnivore that could reach a length of 2 meters.
facts.quote: It was a small, lightly-built, bipedal, ground-dwelling carnivore, and could grow up to 2 m long.

facts.statement: Size estimates indicate Caseosaurus grew up to 2 meters long and weighed no more than 50 kilograms.
facts.quote: Size estimates suggest that Caseosaurus was up to 2 m long and weighed up to 50 kg at most.

facts.statement: The genus name Caseosaurus means "Case's lizard" and honors the scientist Ermine Cowles Case.
facts.quote: The genus name Caseosaurus means "Case's lizard", and was named in honor of the scientist who discovered it, Ermine Cowles Case.

facts.statement: The specific name crosbyensis refers to Crosby County in Texas, where the fossils were discovered.
facts.quote: The specific name crosbyensis, is a Latinized rendering of Crosby County in Texas, the site of its discovery.

facts.statement: The genus was named after Ermine Cowles Case, the scientist who discovered it.
facts.quote: The genus name Caseosaurus means "Case's lizard", and was named in honor of the scientist who discovered it, Ermine Cowles Case.

facts.statement: The sole known specimen of Caseosaurus was found in the Tecovas Formation of the Dockum Group in Texas.
facts.quote: The only specimen of Caseosaurus was discovered in the Tecovas Formation of the Dockum Group in Texas, within sediments deposited during the Norian stage of the Late Triassic period, approximately 221.5 to 212 million years ago.

facts.statement: In 2018, Caseosaurus was re-evaluated as a valid species identified as a relative of Herrerasaurus, placing it outside the Dinosauria.
facts.quote: However, in 2018, Caseosaurus was considered a valid species, and was identified as a relative of Herrerasaurus, outside of the Dinosauria.

facts.statement: In 2004, Langer examined the holotype ilium and reassigned it to the genus Chindesaurus.
facts.quote: Langer (2004) examined the ilium and reassigned it back to the genus Chindesaurus.

facts.statement: Irmis et al. concluded that an ilium originally assigned to Eucoelophysis strongly resembles the Caseosaurus holotype.
facts.quote: Irmis et al. concluded that an ilium, NMMNH P-35995 originally assigned by Heckert et al. in 2000 to the silesaurid Eucoelophysis, strongly resembles the Caseosaurus holotype.

facts.statement: A recent review classified Caseosaurus as a nomen dubium, contradicting earlier studies that validated it.
facts.quote: However, a recent review of early South American dinosaurs has classified it as a nomen dubium without addressing the previous study.

facts.statement: The paleoenvironment of Caseosaurus included the archosaur Tecovasaurus and other early theropods that left preserved bipedal tracks.
facts.quote: The paleoenvironment of Caseosauruss included the archosaur Tecovasaurus and other early theropod dinosaurs, some of which left preserved bipedal tracks.

facts.statement: Caseosaurus is classified within the family Herrerasauridae.
Caseosaurus lived during the Carnian stage of the Late Triassic, approximately 235 to 228 million years ago, in what is now North America.

facts.statement: The genus Caseosaurus is known from specimen UMMP 8870, an isolated hip bone measuring nearly 141 millimeters.
facts.quote: El género Caseosaurus, es conocido por el espécimen UMMP 8870 , un hueso de cadera aislado que mide casi 141 milímetros.

facts.statement: Fossils of Caseosaurus were found in the Dockum Formation of Texas in strata dating to the Upper Triassic.
facts.quote: Sus fósiles fueron hallado en la Formación de Dockum de Texas, en estratos que datan del Triásico superior.

facts.statement: It is possible that Caseosaurus is the same dinosaur as Chindesaurus, another primitive dinosaur from the same period and region.
facts.quote: Puede también que se trate del mismo dinosaurio que Chindesaurus, otro dinosaurio primitivo del mismo período y región geológica.

facts.statement: The only specimen of Caseosaurus was discovered in the Tecovas Formation of the Dockum Group in Texas, in sediments deposited during the Carnian stage of the Upper Triassic, approximately 235 to 228 million years ago.
facts.quote: El único espécimen de Caseosaurus fue descubierto en la Formación Tecovas del Grupo Dockum en Texas, en sedimentos depositados durante la etapa Carniense del Triásico Superior, aproximadamente 235 a 228 millones de años atrás.
